text:
alex: Heads-up — after the kernel update last night we're seeing ~18% p50 regression on host-side parsing path. Traces point at tokenization + gRPC writev bursts (not GPU). Anyone else seeing this? :eyes:

maria: Saw the same on canary. Pulled a flamegraph from the host and tokenization + grpc_writev are hot. Also noticed a lot of small writev calls (~128-512B) rather than coalesced writes. Link to flame (internal): https://perf/reports/4945/flame.svg :chart_with_upwards_trend:

devon: Repro steps I used locally: 
```bash
# replay small-burst workload
wrk -t8 -c200 -d30s --script=small_chunks.lua https://canary.internal/redwood/generate
# collect perf on host
sudo perf record -F 99 -g -p $(pidof redwood-host) -- sleep 20
```
Graphs show host parse loop stalls while waiting for writev to complete.

sam: Noticed KV cache evictions spike around the same time. I think chunk alignment changed: new kernel TCP segmentation + small writev size -> more packets -> increased scheduling jitter -> KV warm paths get preempted. Numbers: evictions 12k->38k/s, kvcache hitrate down 94%->86%.

alex: That matches. So this looks like a host-side IO fragmentation issue cascading to CPU scheduling and kvcache churn. Two-prong: reduce syscall/send fragmentation and adjust batching heuristics to tolerate slightly larger chunk delays.

maria: Quick experiment — increased grpc_write_coalesce window from 0ms -> 1ms in dev shim. Result on canary: small-writev count down 60%, p50 parse back ~10% (not full recovery). Config snippet I used: 
```json
{
  "write_coalesce_ms": 1,
  "max_coalesce_bytes": 4096
}
```
Will push numbers to the dashboard in a min.

devon: Also tried adjusting tokenization thread pool affinity (pin tokenizers to separate CPU set) — that reduced tail jitter but increased average latency for very small requests. Tradeoff log: 
- unpinned p50 22ms p95 140ms
- pinned   p50 25ms p95 110ms
So pinning helps tails but hurts p50 slightly.

sam: For the KV side I ran a quick sim where we align chunk boundaries to 4KB pages before storing in kvcache; eviction rates improved ~30%. That suggests misaligned fragments were thrashing hot shards. Not a long-term fix but promising.

alex: Good. Action items: 1) Maria to extend write_coalesce canary to 2ms and report token writev counts + p50/p95; 2) Devon to test tokenization affinity + measure per-core scheduling jitter; 3) Sam to instrument kvcache shard eviction reasons and add a lightweight 4KB alignment pass; 4) I'll open an ops ticket to roll kernel patch back if canary doesn't stabilize by EOD.

maria: Starting canary change now. Will capture netstat -s and tcp_info to see Nagle/TCP_NODELAY behavior too.

devon: One more datapoint — kernel changelog included a TCP small-queue optimization that reduces coalescing on sockets under 1ms intervals. That aligns with our findings. If we can't adapt at the app layer quickly, we should request a kernel rollback for prod.

ci-bot: Canary deploy queued: parse-canary -> hosts [parse-02, parse-07]. Build: host-opt-2026-03-21.

alex: Thanks — please drop results in this thread. If anyone has a quick patch to grpc shim to buffer until either size threshold OR 1ms, that could be a fast mitigation. Example pseudo-patch: 
```c
// in writev batching loop
if (buffered_bytes < 4096 && elapsed_ms < coalesce_ms) {
  // hold and try to gather more writes
  continue;
}
flush_buffer();
```

maria: Canary @ 2ms done. Initial numbers: small writev calls down 78%, p50 parse recovered ~14%, p95 improved ~22%. kvcache evictions down 25%. Pushing to prod canary group now.

sam: Instrumentation shows fewer preemptions on tokenizer threads after coalesce change. Kernel schedstat still slightly higher than baseline but acceptable.

devon: I'll open an RFC for adding adaptive batching heuristics: prefer coalesce_ms up to 2ms for small requests, but decrease when throughput drops below threshold. Also add a kvcache alignment heuristic and a kvcache hot-shard backpressure.

alex: Great. If prod canary stays green for 2 hours we can ship as a hotfix. Adding owners: maria (coalesce), devon (tokenization affinity + batching RFC), sam (kvcache metrics + alignment).

maria: I'll post the detailed flamegraphs + numbers to the perf dashboard and add links here.

alex: Thanks everyone. Good example of kernel-level change leaking into host-side perf. Keep the thread updated. :thumbsup:
